newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Ford, Opel workers threaten sick pay action.
newsitem.headline: German Ford, Opel workers threaten sick pay action.

text.p: Car workers at Ford and Opel plants in Germany threatened on Monday to strike in protest at controversial rules allowing 20 percent cuts in sick pay which take effect on Tuesday.
Ford Motor Co's German unit Ford-Werke has not yet decided whether to reduce sick pay yet, but a company spokesman said that he expected lightning strikes to go ahead.
The Koelner Stadt-Anzeiger newspaper had reported earlier that the situation on the shop floor was so explosive that walkouts could be held at all Ford's German plants on Tuesday.
Meanwhile, workers at General Motors unit Adam Opel AG's Bochum plant will strike on all three shifts on Tuesday if managers decide to impose the cuts, local IG Metall union chief Ludgar Hinse said.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government passed the sick pay cuts through parliament just over two weeks back as part of a major round of welfare cuts and austerity measures intended to boost job creation and restore competitiveness.
But Germany's industrial peace has been shattered by a rush by some big firms, led by auto giant Daimler-Benz AG, to impose the sick pay cuts from October 1.

Outraged union leaders say full sick pay is written into their work contracts. They called out over 20,000 workers from extra weekend shifts at three of Daimler's Mercedes plants, and further protests are planned at the plants on Tuesday.
